sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
sources.officialityEvidence: The Federal Ministry of Justice publishes the constitutional text on its official justice.gov.ng domain; section 41 controls a Nigerian citizen's entry right.
sources.supportingExcerpt: No citizen of Nigeria shall be expelled from Nigeria or refused entry thereby or exit therefrom.

sources.title: Nigeria Immigration Service Service Level Agreement: revised edition April 2026
sources.officialityEvidence: NIS publishes this revised April 2026 SLA on immigration.gov.ng. It specifies F5A's electronic process, purpose, duration and expressly reserved nationality exceptions.
sources.supportingExcerpt: except ECOWAS member States and other countries with which Nigeria has entered into visa abolition/waiver agreements

sources.title: Nigeria Immigration Service: What is the Nigeria e-Visa?
sources.officialityEvidence: This current NIS FAQ on immigration.gov.ng describes the electronically issued approval, rather than merely online form filing.
sources.supportingExcerpt: eligible foreign nationals to apply for and receive a Nigerian visa electronically

sources.title: Nigeria Immigration Service: Who is eligible for the Nigeria e-Visa?
sources.officialityEvidence: NIS publishes this current nationality-eligibility FAQ. It expressly warns that bilateral agreements or reciprocity can require in-person processing.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Many nationalities can apply for an e-Visa, but some may still require in-person applications.

sources.title: Nigeria Immigration Service Landing and Exit Card
sources.officialityEvidence: The live NIS service identifies NIS headquarters and contact details and separately classifies ECOWAS passports for the landing-card process.

sources.title: ECOWAS Protocol A/P.1/5/79 relating to free movement of persons, residence and establishment
sources.publisher: Economic Community of West African States
sources.officialityEvidence: ECOWAS currently hosts the Protocol from its official domain. Article 3 gives Community citizens the short-visit visa exemption.
sources.supportingExcerpt: A citizen of the Community visiting any Member State for a period not exceeding ninety days shall enter free of visa requirements.

sources.title: ECOWAS current Member States
sources.publisher: Economic Community of West African States
sources.officialityEvidence: The Commission's live official page identifies the current 12-member cohort, including Nigeria.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Benin, Cabo Verde, Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea Bissau, Liberia, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone, The Gambia, Togo.

sources.title: ECOWAS press statement on Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger withdrawal
sources.publisher: Economic Community of West African States
sources.officialityEvidence: The ECOWAS Commission's official 29 January 2025 statement expressly preserves the three withdrawn States' free-movement rights until further notice.
sources.supportingExcerpt: allow citizens of the three affected countries to continue to enjoy the right of visa free movement

policies.title: Nigerian ordinary passport: citizenship/home entry
policies.summary: Constitution section 41 prevents refusal of entry to a Nigerian citizen. This normalizes the NG ordinary-passport home cell only.
conditions: This is a citizenship/home-entry normalization, not a visitor visa or a rule for dual nationals travelling only on another State's passport.
Lawful identity/document checks and any constitutionally permitted restriction remain outside this visitor-status label.

policies.title: ECOWAS and continuing AES ordinary passports: Nigeria short-visit visa exemption
policies.summary: The live NIS landing-card service labels ECOWAS passports visa-free/exempt. The ECOWAS Protocol exempts Community citizens from visa requirements for visits up to 90 days, and ECOWAS expressly continues that right for Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger until further notice.
conditions: The Protocol baseline requires a valid travel document and international health certificate, is limited to a visit not exceeding 90 days, and does not displace Nigeria's admission, security, health or documentary checks.
Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger withdrew on 29 January 2025; ECOWAS's transition statement continues their visa-free movement until further notice and requires current rechecking.
This maps ordinary-passport short visitor movement only; it does not cover ECOWAS travel certificates, residence, establishment, employment, transit or special-passport routes.
The Landing and Exit Card is a border declaration process, not an ETA or visa.
